title: Genome-wide association study and predictors of neonatal blood cell traits in Hispanic newborns.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran paper_context.py: Europe PMC full text returned HTTP 500, the supplementary-files endpoint returned no zip, and no GEO/Zenodo/Dryad records were found. NCBI elink gives one dbGaP (database of Genotypes and Phenotypes, a controlled-access human genetics archive) link, ID 2787135; its esummary returned 'cannot get document summary'.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: From the abstract only: 382 Hispanic newborns, 24 flow-cytometry blood cell traits measured in cord blood, six significant loci, and effects of C-section delivery and sex.

a1_downloadable.note: The only data link is a dbGaP record, which is controlled access and needs an application. No open files were found. Checked through NCBI links, not by opening any file.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not verified. Per the abstract, the 24 cell-type proportions measured by flow cytometry would be measured columns.

a3_inputs_present.note: The inputs would be individual genotypes, which sit behind controlled access. Not checked in files.

a4_units_stated.note: Not verified. The paper's description suggests cell proportions.

a5_enough_rows.note: 382 newborns, the number given in the abstract and not checked in files. That is far below the ~1,500 threshold for regression.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: unknown; genotype array for 382 people is likely <1 GB

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Could not check, because no files were accessible.

a8_label_provenance.note: Per the abstract, the labels are flow-cytometry measurements, not model outputs. Not verified.

honest_claim_h3: Among 382 Hispanic newborns from one cohort, genotype plus birth factors explain part of the variation in cord-blood immune cell proportions.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use newborn genotypes, delivery mode and sex to predict immune cell proportions in cord blood.
plain_idea.train_on: Genetic variants plus birth details for each newborn; 382 newborns according to the abstract (not verified).
plain_idea.predict: The fraction of each of 24 blood cell types, measured by flow cytometry (laser-based cell counting) of cord blood.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Researchers studying newborn immunity would learn how much of immune makeup at birth is inherited, but 382 samples are far too few for ML.

ml_idea: Predict cord-blood immune cell composition from genotype and birth covariates. This is not viable with 382 controlled-access samples.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated, because no data was accessible.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Look for any open individual-level table; none was found. The only data link is dbGaP.

verdict_reason: Fails A1 and A5. The individual-level data is only in dbGaP (controlled access, needs an application), and the cohort has 382 newborns, far below the ~1,500 rows needed. Both facts come from NCBI links and the abstract; no files were opened.
